record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.context_brief: Incenters on Euler lines of simplices
record.original_question: For n >= 3, geometrically characterize the n-simplices in Euclidean n-space E^n whose incenter lies on their Euler line, where the Euler line for such a simplex is the affine hull of its circumcenter and centroid.

evidence.quote: Question 9. Characterize geometrically those n-simplices in En, n >= 3, for which the incenter lies on the Euler line.
No analogous characterization is known for n-simplices in En (n >= 3) whose incenter I lies on their Euler line, which still is the affine hull of C and S.

artifact.status_search_result: Standard references confirm the planar characterization (incenter on Euler line iff the triangle is isosceles), but no analogous geometric characterization for n-simplices in E^n with n ≥ 3 was located in available sources. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Euler line - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The incenter generally does not lie on the Euler line; it is on the Euler line only for isosceles triangles.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the n=2 characterization but no higher-dimensional analogue is given.

status_evidence.title: A Simplex Contained in a Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of centers (centroid, circumcenter) of higher-dimensional simplices.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional simplex center literature does not provide a geometric characterization of when the incenter lies on the Euler line.
